# TorontoHealth
> Dated, checkable evidence on Growth Guys discount codes and third-party peptide lab reports, for buyers in Canada. Every figure is produced by a guest-cart test or read from a laboratory report that resolves on that laboratory's own domain. Research use only; not medical advice.

## Verification evidence
> Dated cart tests, the hash-chained ledger, the protocol, the assay index and the corrections log.

- [Assay reports — 244 published, 33 below 98% | Toronto Health Source](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/lab-reports.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/lab-reports.md)): 244 third-party assay reports, average 99.03% purity, with the 33 results below 98% left visible and the lowest at 93.844%.
- [Cart ledger — 133 hash-chained HEALTHYLIFE10 tests | Toronto Health Source](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/ledger.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/ledger.md)): Every HEALTHYLIFE10 cart test, 2026-08-30 to 2026-10-09, each entry chained by SHA-256 to the one before it so the series cannot be rewritten after the fact.
- [Corrections — errors we published, and when we fixed them | Toronto Health Source](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/corrections.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/corrections.md)): A dated list of figures we got wrong and have since corrected. Entries are added, never removed.
- [How we verify — the cart test protocol | Toronto Health Source](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/how-we-verify.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/how-we-verify.md)): The exact steps of the automated cart test behind every figure we publish, the basket values it uses, and the things the method cannot establish.
- [The HEALTHYLIFE10 Verification Log — 133 dated cart tests, hash-chained](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/evidence/index.md)): Every HEALTHYLIFE10 cart test we have run, 133 of them across 41 days, chained so the series cannot be rewritten. Plus 244 third-party assay reports and what none of it establishes.

Change one variable at a time to tell which.

- [Sample Size, and What a Small Study Cannot Tell You](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/sample-size-and-what-it-limits.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/sample-size-and-what-it-limits.md)): Sample size governs precision, not correctness. A small study is compatible with a wide range of true effects, which is why its striking headline figure is weaker evidence than it looks.

When, against what, and what happened on failure are the questions that separate them.

- [What Mass Spectrometry Adds That Purity Does Not](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/mass-spectrometry-in-peptide-testing.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/mass-spectrometry-in-peptide-testing.md)): Mass spectrometry answers identity: it weighs the molecule and compares that against the mass calculated for the compound on the label. Purity cannot answer that.

- [What a Purity Percentage Does and Does Not Measure](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/purity-is-not-potency.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/purity-is-not-potency.md)): A purity percentage says what proportion of a sample was the named compound. It is not a measure of effect, of dose delivered, or of how much is in the vial.

Without one a figure is a reading rather than a measurement, and cross-lab comparison breaks.

A hash-chained record proves it has not been edited since — and a reader can recompute it without trusting anyone.

What it is made of matters more than the percentage.

- [Why Research Peptides Ship as a Dry Powder](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-peptides-ship-lyophilised.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-peptides-ship-lyophilised.md)): Water is what degrades a peptide fastest, so the water is removed before shipping — which is also why a diluent is a separate purchase and why the vial can look empty.
- [Why Two Percentage Discounts Compound Instead of Adding](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-percentages-compound.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-percentages-compound.md)): Two percentage discounts usually do not add: the second is normally taken from what the first left, so 7% and 11% come to 17.23% rather than 18%. The exception is a store that computes both against the original subtotal as separate lines, where they do add — which is observable on the order itself.

A date alone is not enough either — the figures have to move with it.

- [Why a Lab Set With No Weak Results Should Worry You](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-a-published-set-with-no-weak-results-is-suspect.html) ([markdown](https://growthguyscanada.ca/guides/why-a-published-set-with-no-weak-results-is-suspect.md)): Read a published lab set for its worst result, not its average. A set with no weak results in it has been filtered, and tells you about the filter rather than the products.
